headline: Amherst outscores the conference and stands alone
dek: Amherst has scored 48 goals across all matches, more than any other NESCAC program, while conceding 25. Its eleven wins, seven draws, and four defeats have carried it past Williams and left it as the lone conference side with a match still to come.

pattern.label: derived
pattern.text: Attacking output splits sharply across the conference: Amherst has paired 48 goals with 25 conceded, outscoring Colby and Bates combined.

wire.line: Conference sides have 57 wins, ten draws, and six defeats against non-conference opponents, scoring 202 goals and conceding 51.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Hamilton accounts for the conference's one match past its date with no published result, against Mohawk Valley Community.

findings.label: derived
findings.text: Williams finished with fourteen wins, three draws, and three defeats, more victories than any other NESCAC program.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Middlebury has spread its 42 goals across at least eighteen distinct scorers while conceding twelve.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Amherst freshman defender Edward Wilkey has scored eight goals and added one assist from 28 shots.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Tufts goalkeeper Nikola Antic made 77 saves while conceding thirteen goals, for a 0.856 save percentage.

last_match.line: Amherst took the result after a loss and a draw in earlier meetings, and remains the lone NESCAC program still on the schedule.

next_match.line: St. Olaf already won at Tufts, while Amherst enters as the conference's highest-scoring program.

validation.policy: observed and derived claims are recomputed against the data home before publish; failures are dropped, not softened. signal and projected pass on schema unless the data contradicts a figure. context is never validated as a finding.
